title: feat: immutable payment_audit_log table and write service
author: arjun.mehta
description:
Implements the immutable payment_audit_log table and audit write service (NEX-219). PCI-DSS Level 1 requirement: log all access to cardholder data.

Schema:
```sql
CREATE TABLE payment_audit_log (
  id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY,
  event_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  stripe_event_id VARCHAR(255),
  user_id UUID,
  amount INTEGER,
  currency CHAR(3),
  status VARCHAR(50),
  ip_address INET,
  metadata JSONB,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

ALTER TABLE payment_audit_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY audit_log_insert_only ON payment_audit_log FOR INSERT TO payments_service WITH CHECK (true);
```

Partitioned by month using the partitioning pattern established in NEX-189 (Diana Chen's database migration).

Audit service: writes synchronously before any business logic. If the audit write fails, the entire transaction is aborted — we never process a payment without an audit record.

Related: NEX-219, NEX-204, NEX-189, architecture_review_01, pci-dss-compliance.md

review_comments.author: diana.chen
review_comments.comment: Partitioning by month is the right call — consistent with the events table pattern from NEX-189. The RLS policy looks correct. One thing: make sure the partition creation job is automated, otherwise we'll need a manual step each month.

review_comments.author: arjun.mehta
review_comments.comment: Good catch Diana — added a pg_cron job to create next month's partition on the 25th of each month.
